summary.text: Kamillah Hanks was elected in 2021 to represent the 49th District on the New York City Council, which covers Staten Island's North Shore.
Her Council biography says that in January 2026 she was appointed Majority Whip, the first Staten Islander in that leadership role.

paragraphs.text: Hanks is a lifelong Staten Islander with a background in marketing and finance from the College of Staten Island, according to her Council biography.
In 2012 she founded the Historic Tappen Park Community Partnership and she established Staten Island's first YouthBuild program, which secured a $1.1 million U.S. Department of Labor grant in 2018.

During the COVID-19 pandemic she partnered with local businesses and YouthBuild participants to produce and donate more than 5,000 face shields, and in 2020 she founded the Minority Women in Business Association of Staten Island.

The biography says she has delivered more than $98 million in funding for schools, parks, health care and community initiatives and worked to secure $426 million for the North Shore waterfront project.
